key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the onset of plastic flow by slowing early deformation, with chemistry playing the dominant role over boundary relaxation.
engineering_relevance: Tuning grain-boundary composition in nanocrystalline stainless steels could improve resistance to early plasticity and raise flow strength under loading.
method: Hybrid MD/MC simulations on three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Compared segregated, annealed, and random controls using the same microstructures
Evaluated uniaxial creep/loading at 4.6 GPa and fixed strain-rate tests across 300, 750, and 950 K
evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals took about 16% longer to reach 50% strain than random controls, and showed a 6–7% higher peak stress at fixed strain rate across all tested temperatures.
watch_item: The observed Cr enrichment depends on how the reference region is defined, so segregation conclusions should be interpreted carefully when comparing fcc-only versus far-field grain-interior references.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
